close_reason: Fixed in 4fac15e. Trait signature widened from Output=bool to Output=Result<bool, Self::Error>. Handler at addressbook.rs maps Err -> serverFail via server_fail_value_from_backend. MemoryBackend (in-memory, infallible) wraps the existing computation in Ok(); test_support MockBackend gains set_fail_has_contents() knob and a new regression test exercises the Err -> serverFail path. Trait doc explicitly forbids fail-open by returning Ok(false) on storage degradation. README updated. 94+28+1 contacts-server tests pass; workspace clippy + tests clean. Does not propagate to canonical mail-server (no analogous RFC 8621 method).
description:
LOCATION: crate-jmap-contacts-server/src/backend.rs:100-110

SIGNATURE:
    fn address_book_has_contents(
        &self,
        caller: &Self::CallerCtx,
        account_id: &jmap_types::Id,
        address_book_id: &jmap_types::Id,
    ) -> impl std::future::Future<Output = bool> + Send;

PROBLEM:
Every other read/write method on ContactsBackend and its JmapBackend
supertrait returns Result<_, Self::Error>. This one returns plain bool.
A backend cannot signal a storage error from this call. Three things
go wrong for the caller:

1. **Fail-open silent data loss.** If the backend is degraded (DB
   connection lost, replica unreachable, query timeout) and cannot
   determine whether the AddressBook has contents, the backend MUST
   return either `true` (over-conservative, blocks all destroys) or
   `false` (fail-open: destroys proceed against possibly-non-empty
   books, silently violating the RFC 9610 §3 addressBookHasContents
   contract). A real backend that fails-open will lose contact data the
   first time the storage layer flaps.

2. **No serverFail propagation.** Every other contacts handler path
   maps backend errors to JMAP `serverFail` via
   `jmap_server::server_fail_from_backend(&e)`. This one path cannot
   participate — the handler at addressbook.rs:266-269 has no error to
   propagate. The destroy outcome becomes ambiguous to the client.

3. **Trait future-pinning.** Once we ship `Output = bool`, switching to
   `Output = Result<bool, Self::Error>` is a breaking change for every
   backend implementor. The convenient and correct contract is
   permanently unreachable without a major-version bump.

EVIDENCE FROM HANDLER (crate-jmap-contacts-server/src/addressbook.rs):

    if !on_destroy_remove_contents
        && backend
            .address_book_has_contents(caller, &account_id, &id)
            .await   // ← unconditional bool, no error path
    {
        not_destroyed.insert(id_str, set_error_value(...));
        continue;
    }

The MemoryBackend reference impl at memory.rs:794-805 uses `.unwrap_or(false)`
on a missing aux entry, embodying exactly the silent fail-open this
trait shape forces. A production backend that has to query a relational
DB has no better option.

WHAT CALLERS CANNOT DEPEND ON:
- That a backend storage failure surfaces as `serverFail` to the JMAP
  client.
- That `false` means "definitely empty" rather than "couldn't determine".
- That the answer is causally connected to the storage state at all.

RECOMMENDED:
Change the signature to:
    fn address_book_has_contents(
        &self,
        caller: &Self::CallerCtx,
        account_id: &Id,
        address_book_id: &Id,
    ) -> impl Future<Output = Result<bool, Self::Error>> + Send;

The handler maps Err(e) to `server_fail_from_backend(&e)` via the
existing path and returns the resulting JmapError as a method-level
error (consistent with how account_exists Err is handled at
addressbook.rs:73-79).

PARENT-EPIC RELATIONSHIP:
This is the trait-shape angle on the same concern as JMAP-qz9v.1
(README documents cascade that the code does not implement). Even if
JMAP-qz9v.1 is fixed by implementing the cascade, the bool return type
makes a correct fix impossible without a breaking change. Fix this one
FIRST while the crate is at 0.1.x.

PROPAGATION: the canonical sibling jmap-mail-server has no analog (no
RFC 8621 method needs an analogous "has contents" check), so this fix
does not propagate.
title: ContactsBackend::address_book_has_contents returns bool not Result — backend cannot signal storage error, must fail-open
